name: GazeRing
summary: A pressure-sensing ring on the index finger works with gaze: a long press opens a cone around the gaze, thumb slides or taps on the ring refine the cone and step through the objects in it by depth, and another long press selects.
howItWorks: On a HoloLens 2, a flexible pressure sensor on a ring is operated by the thumb in two modes: sliding in eight directions (GR-S) or tapping five areas (GR-T). A 1.5 s press opens a 6° gaze cone; sliding or tapping shifts it to correct eye-tracking error; up and down step through the objects inside by depth, making the others transparent; a long press confirms. The hand can stay out of the cameras' view. With 16 participants, both GazeRing modes were faster than gaze-and-speech and gaze dwell when targets were occluded or eye tracking was off by 2–3°, and GR-T was preferred.
